whyThisMatters: Real security moments offshore are fast, with limited time online — you don't get time to research if a link, a call, or a request is safe. This game trains your reflex for good habits, and helps you catch things that only sound safe.
rememberThis: This month's habit to carry forward: fast instinct is good, but some things only sound safe — a familiar-sounding voice, correct vessel details, an urgent deadline. When you are not sure, slow down and check before you trust the label.

discussionPrompts: Ask the group which bubble tricked them. Most people get at least one of the trick bubbles wrong on their first try.
Ask why a familiar-sounding voice on a call isn't proof of who's really calling.
Ask why taking longer to respond with limited signal is listed as a good habit here, not a delay to worry about.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: The most common mistake is tapping anything that sounds confident or familiar — a voice that sounds official, correct vessel details, an urgent deadline — without checking it through a channel you already trust. The trick bubbles are there to catch that habit.

bubbles.text: Press and hold a link to preview it
bubbles.why: Previewing the real address shows if a link goes somewhere fake.

bubbles.text: Report unknown USB sticks
bubbles.why: Unknown USB sticks can carry malware, so security should handle them.

bubbles.text: Hang up and call a known number
bubbles.why: Calling a trusted number reaches the real person, not the impostor.

bubbles.text: Use the known secure agent portal
bubbles.why: The official portal is protected; a link sent to you may be a fake.

bubbles.text: Verify fund requests on a known number
bubbles.why: A trusted number exposes fake money requests before funds are sent.

bubbles.text: Check the sender on rotation emails
bubbles.why: Fake crew-change emails use look-alike domains to steal details or money.

bubbles.text: Leave unknown devices unplugged
bubbles.why: Unknown devices can install malware the moment you plug them in.

bubbles.text: Open the crew portal from a bookmark
bubbles.why: A bookmark takes you to the real site, not a look-alike that steals logins.

bubbles.text: Report suspicious text messages
bubbles.why: Reporting helps warn the rest of the crew before someone falls for it.

bubbles.text: Escalate urgent unverified requests
bubbles.why: Scammers rely on speed; passing it on gets the request properly checked.

bubbles.text: Tap a rotation link unchecked
bubbles.why: Fake crew-change links lead to sites that steal your login or details.

bubbles.text: Plug in an unknown USB stick
bubbles.why: A found USB stick can install malware on the ship's systems.

bubbles.text: Give your password over the phone
bubbles.why: Real IT staff never ask for passwords; callers who do are after your account.

bubbles.text: Email a passport scan to a contact
bubbles.why: Passport scans in email can be stolen and used for identity theft.

bubbles.text: Buy gift cards to pay port dues
bubbles.why: Gift card payments are untraceable and are a favourite scam request.

bubbles.text: Sign a renewal under deadline pressure
bubbles.why: Pressure to sign quickly is a tactic to stop you reading what you agree to.

bubbles.text: Trust a caller who sounds official
bubbles.why: Criminals sound convincing; sounding official doesn't prove who is calling.

bubbles.text: Ignore a wrong crew portal address
bubbles.why: A web address that doesn't match is a sign of a fake login page.

bubbles.text: Share a verification code on a call
bubbles.why: Verification codes let attackers into your account if you share them.

bubbles.text: Skip checking where a link goes
bubbles.why: Unchecked links can lead to fake sites that steal your details.

bubbles.text: Verify the sender, not just vessel name
bubbles.why: Scammers research real vessel names, so a correct name proves nothing.

bubbles.text: Take time to verify, even offshore
bubbles.why: Limited signal is no reason to rush; scammers exploit it to hurry you.

bubbles.text: Trust a voice that sounds familiar
bubbles.why: Voices can be copied, so sounding familiar doesn't prove who is calling.

bubbles.text: Call the number given in a text
bubbles.why: The number in a scam text connects you to the scammer, not the real company.
